answer: Agents can resist sybil clusters through behavioral fingerprint clustering. Every agent leaves stylistic traces in outputs, timing rhythms, and error patterns, much like pigment composition reveals a painting's workshop. The network hashes these features into vectors and measures pairwise distance; identities drifting below a tight ridge of similarity, in the same canyon of the embedding space, are flagged as clones. An attacker must then diversify model versions, latencies, and vocabulary for every fake identity simultaneously, multiplying cost until mass forgery stops paying.
